entities.summary:
Conchobar mac Tadg, King of Connacht 967–973, played a pivotal role in shaping the medieval landscape of Ireland. His reign was marked by significant military campaigns against the Vikings, which led to the expansion of Connacht's influence and the eventual establishment of the O'Conor family's dominance. The O'Conor family's strategic alliances with other Irish kingdoms and their efforts to resist Norman invasion also had far-reaching consequences for the medieval Irish polity. Conchobar mac Tadg's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his successors continued to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined medieval Ireland.

Conchobar mac Tadg was born of unknown parentage and died in 973 CE, leaving behind a dynasty that would shape the history of Connacht for centuries to come. His eponymous descendants would become one of Ireland's most prominent families, and their name would be invoked in medieval texts as a symbol of power and prestige.

The impact of Conchobar mac Tadg's reign can be seen in the many place names and cultural artifacts that still bear his name today, from the town of Connaught to the O'Conor family's ancestral seat at Turlough.

In the annals of medieval Irish history, Conchobar mac Tadg stands as a testament to the enduring power of local dynasties and the complex, often tumultuous, nature of medieval Irish politics.
